title: Accessibility Policy: Service Animals and Cleaning and Damage Fees
content:
Hair or dander shed by a service animal is never charged as a Cleaning and Damage Fees charge: a report of animal hair or mess that consists of shedding from a service animal the rider was travelling with is denied before charge, or reversed in full with the refund reason service animal shedding when already charged.

Whether the animal was a service animal is the rider's own statement and is accepted as given; the rider is never asked for documentation or the animal's training.

A mess other than shedding left by a service animal is charged at its level like any other mess.

## Where each fact comes from

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| The incident category of the report, and the assessment concerned | the assessment record |
| That the animal was a service animal | the rider's own statement, accepted as given |

## Outcomes

| What the report shows | Not yet charged | Already charged |
|---|---|---|
| Shedding (hair or dander) from a service animal the rider was travelling with | denied before charge | reversed in full, refund reason service animal shedding |
| A mess other than shedding left by a service animal | charged at its level like any other mess | treated like any other fee charged at its level |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A rider disputes a charged animal hair fee and says the dog travelling with them was a service animal; the photos show shed hair on the rear seat. The rider's statement is accepted as given, nothing further is asked about the animal, and the fee is reversed in full with the reason service animal shedding.
